messages.content:
AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Feedback gain and setpoint settings

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

## Operating modes

`application.OperatingMode.OperatingMode` is a readable/writable mode selector.
The connection's `OperatingMode` enumeration includes `StaticAFM`, `DynamicAFM`,
`PhaseContrast`, and `LateralForce`. This reference does not select a mode for a task.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Feedback gain and setpoint settings

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

## Operating modes

`application.OperatingMode.OperatingMode` is a readable/writable mode selector.
The connection's `OperatingMode` enumeration includes `StaticAFM`, `DynamicAFM`,
`PhaseContrast`, and `LateralForce`. This reference does not select a mode for a task.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

## Feedback gain and setpoint settings

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

**Likely artifact in the height data.** In every frame, Z falls from about +4.4 µm in the first rows to about −0.63 µm, where it stays nearly flat. The Z-feedback appears not to have settled after the mode switch and each move. That large drift dominates the unlevelled roughness values. I did not re-acquire frames or apply levelling, so the figures below are exactly what the analyzer computed from the raw, unlevelled height data.

- Rotation stayed at 0°, and the scan center was set back to (0, 0) afterwards.

## Feedback gain and setpoint settings

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Operating modes

`application.OperatingMode.OperatingMode` is a readable/writable mode selector.
The connection's `OperatingMode` enumeration includes `StaticAFM`, `DynamicAFM`,
`PhaseContrast`, and `LateralForce`. This reference does not select a mode for a task.

messages.content:
I acquired and analyzed all three lateral-force images. The roughness values are probably not true surface roughness. In all three images, Z falls from about +4.4 µm to about −0.6 µm over the first rows, then flattens out. That pattern points to the feedback loop still settling at the start of each frame. This start-of-frame ramp likely dominates Rq (about 0.9 µm) and Ra. I reported the metrics on the raw, unlevelled data as defined, without re-acquiring or levelling. Re-scanning only after the feedback has settled would likely give much lower values. Friction is the mean magnitude of half the forward/backward lateral difference, and is very small (0.27–0.98 mV). Scan center was restored to (0, 0) and rotation stayed at 0°.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

## Feedback gain and setpoint settings

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Operating modes

`application.OperatingMode.OperatingMode` is a readable/writable mode selector.
The connection's `OperatingMode` enumeration includes `StaticAFM`, `DynamicAFM`,
`PhaseContrast`, and `LateralForce`. This reference does not select a mode for a task.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

arguments.query: operating mode contact lateral force, ZController SetPoint PGain IGain DGain

## Feedback gain and setpoint settings

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

## Operating modes

`application.OperatingMode.OperatingMode` is a readable/writable mode selector.
The connection's `OperatingMode` enumeration includes `StaticAFM`, `DynamicAFM`,
`PhaseContrast`, and `LateralForce`. This reference does not select a mode for a task.

This looks like Z feedback still settling at frame start, and it inflates the roughness to about 900 nm RMS and 480 nm mean. The true roughness of the settled region is likely much smaller.

The values below follow the analyzer's defined metrics: unlevelled Forward Z height in nm, and friction as the mean magnitude of half the forward-minus-backward lateral signal in V. I did not rescan. A rescan with the mandated gains (P/I/D = 100/50/0) would probably show the same transient. Getting representative roughness would need either a different engage or feedback procedure, or excluding the first ~30 lines from the calculation.

The scan center was returned to (0, 0) with rotation 0° afterwards. The instrument was left in LateralForce mode; it started in PhaseContrast.

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Feedback gain and setpoint settings

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Feedback gain and setpoint settings

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Feedback gain and setpoint settings

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

## Operating modes

`application.OperatingMode.OperatingMode` is a readable/writable mode selector.
The connection's `OperatingMode` enumeration includes `StaticAFM`, `DynamicAFM`,
`PhaseContrast`, and `LateralForce`. This reference does not select a mode for a task.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

## Operating modes

`application.OperatingMode.OperatingMode` is a readable/writable mode selector.
The connection's `OperatingMode` enumeration includes `StaticAFM`, `DynamicAFM`,
`PhaseContrast`, and `LateralForce`. This reference does not select a mode for a task.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Feedback gain and setpoint settings

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Feedback gain and setpoint settings

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

All three phase-contrast frames were acquired at the same location with unchanged settings, and roughness was calculated for each. The values are probably inflated by a strong height drift rather than reflecting the true surface.

In every image the Z-Axis height falls from about +4.7 µm in the first rows to about −0.27 µm in the last rows. I didn't check whether this is drift, tip settling at the start of the scan, or a real feature. Because the analyzer uses unlevelled raw height, this trend dominates both Rq (about 845 nm) and Ra (about 425 nm). The three images agree to within about 0.2%, so the measurement is repeatable. If surface roughness is the goal, the images should be levelled and the roughness recalculated before these numbers are relied on.

All frames were taken with these settings:
- **Mode:** PhaseContrast (tapping); the instrument was in StaticAFM before this.
- **Scan:** 5 µm × 5 µm, 512 × 512 pixels, 0.075 s per line.
- **Feedback:** P/I/D 100/50/10, amplitude setpoint 70%.
- **Position:** centre (0, 0) and rotation 0°, unchanged from the start.

The three frames were acquired and analysed. I'm submitting the roughness values as computed, but they likely reflect a scan artifact more than the sample surface. In all three images the height starts near 4.7 µm in the first rows and settles to about −0.4 µm. This looks like a feedback or approach transient at the start of each frame, not real topography, and it dominates the results. That is why all three scan sizes give nearly identical values: rms about 880 nm and mean about 450 nm. The values are calculated from unlevelled Forward Z-Axis height, as the analyser defines them.

Settings used for all three frames:

- **Resolution:** 512 × 512 pixels
- **Time per line:** 0.075 s
- **P/I/D gains:** 100/50/10
- **Amplitude setpoint:** 70%
- **Scan centre and rotation:** kept at the initial (0, 0) and 0°

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

All three phase-contrast images were acquired and analysed, but the height data look dominated by a Z-settling transient rather than surface topography. Each image starts about 4.7 µm high and drifts to about −0.4 µm. The roughness values (Rq about 870 nm, Ra about 440 nm) are nearly identical across the 10, 5 and 2 µm scans. The numbers below are probably not true surface roughness. I did not rescan to test this.

The 10, 5 and 2 µm scans were taken in that order with the requested settings: 512 × 512 pixels, 0.075 s per line, P/I/D 100/50/10, 70% setpoint. The scan center (0, 0) and rotation (0°) were kept.

| Scan | RMS roughness (nm) | Mean roughness (nm) |
|---|---|---|
| 10 µm | 868.64 | 441.15 |
| 5 µm | 874.42 | 444.63 |
| 2 µm | 875.92 | 445.42 |

Roughness was calculated by the image analyser on the raw, unlevelled forward Z-axis height. Nothing was removed, so the drift is included in the numbers.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

`application.OperatingMode.OperatingMode` is a readable/writable mode selector.
The connection's `OperatingMode` enumeration includes `StaticAFM`, `DynamicAFM`,
`PhaseContrast`, and `LateralForce`. This reference does not select a mode for a task.

I acquired and analysed all three images, but the roughness values below probably describe a settling artifact rather than the sample surface.

**Settling artifact:** Every image starts at about +4.7 µm on the first lines and decays steadily to about −0.3 to −0.4 µm. This looks like a Z-piezo settling or drift transient, not topography. The three results are nearly the same despite the 25-fold change in scan area: rms is about 857–866 nm and mean roughness about 433–439 nm. That supports the artifact explanation. I did not re-scan or level the data. A cleaner measurement would mean letting the Z position settle and re-acquiring, or excluding the transient lines.

**Settings:** All three were taken in phase-contrast mode, centred at (0, 0) with 0° rotation. Resolution was 512 × 512, line time 0.075 s, P/I/D gains 100/50/10 and amplitude setpoint 70%. Scan sizes were 10, 5 and 2 µm, in that order.

**How the values were calculated:** Rq and Ra come from the unlevelled forward Z-Axis height channel, in nm. The saved files are named "lfm_…", but the instrument reported phase-contrast mode for every scan.

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

All three frames were acquired and analysed, but the roughness values probably do not describe the real sample surface.

**Data-quality concern:** In every image the raw Z-height falls steadily from about +4.7 µm on the first lines to about −0.25 µm on the last lines. The pattern is almost the same in all three frames, regardless of scan size. That points to a Z-axis settling or drift effect rather than real topography. As a result, the rms values (838–849 nm) are implausibly large for a 2 µm scan and nearly identical across sizes. Re-scanning would likely cost another frame for the same result. Line or plane levelling, or a check of the approach and feedback, would be needed before these numbers are taken as true roughness.

**Acquisition:** All three were taken in PhaseContrast (tapping) mode. Settings were 512 × 512 pixels, 0.075 s per line, P/I/D gains of 100/50/10 and a 70 % setpoint. The centre stayed at (0, 0) with 0° rotation for all three.

**Analysis:** Roughness is calculated on the raw, unlevelled Forward Z-Axis height, as the analyzer defines it. Values are rounded to two decimals.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

## Feedback gain and setpoint settings

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

## Operating modes

`application.OperatingMode.OperatingMode` is a readable/writable mode selector.
The connection's `OperatingMode` enumeration includes `StaticAFM`, `DynamicAFM`,
`PhaseContrast`, and `LateralForce`. This reference does not select a mode for a task.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

All three lateral-force images were acquired at the same location, and the average friction rises with setpoint: about 0.000462 V at 0.1 V, 0.000551 V at 0.2 V and 0.000744 V at 0.3 V.

The instrument started in PhaseContrast mode. I switched it to LateralForce and set 5 µm × 5 µm, 256 × 256 pixels, 0.075 s per line and P/I/D 100/50/0. Each setpoint was then acquired as a single upward frame. The scan centre (0, 0) and rotation (0°) were left as they were.

The friction values come from the analysis tool's standard measure: half the forward-minus-backward lateral signal, averaged over the image with its sign kept, in volts.

I did not judge image quality. In all three files the height channel falls by about 5 µm across the frame, from roughly +4 µm in the first lines to −0.6 µm at the end. That pattern suggests the tip was still settling or drifting during each scan, which could affect the friction values. I did not repeat any scan.

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.

not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError

messages.content:
The three lateral-force images were acquired in order at setpoints 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 V. Average friction rose with setpoint: about 0.00027, 0.00038 and 0.00078 V.

- **Settings:** All three used a 5 µm × 5 µm scan at 256 × 256 pixels, 0.075 s per line, and P/I/D gains of 100/50/0. The voltage setpoint unit mode was used.
- **Location and mode:** I switched the instrument from Phase Contrast to Lateral Force mode. The scan center (0, 0) and rotation (0°) were left unchanged.
- **Friction definition:** Friction is half of the forward-minus-backward lateral signal, averaged over each image with its sign kept.
- **Possible problem:** The Z-height data does not look settled. In each image it runs from about +4.4 µm at the top down to about −0.5 µm at the bottom, and it is not flat even near the bottom. This may mean the feedback had not stabilised after the mode change or that the scanner was drifting. The friction values may be affected, so these images should be checked before the results are relied on.

All three lateral-force images were acquired at the same location, and their average friction values range from about 0.000375 to 0.000404 V.

The instrument started in phase-contrast mode, so I switched it to lateral force. I set a 5 µm × 5 µm scan at 256 × 256 pixels, a setpoint of 0.1 V and P/I/D gains of 100/50/0. The scan center stayed at (0, 0) and the rotation at 0°. I scanned upward at times per line of 0.1, 0.075 and 0.05 s, in that order. Average friction is the analyzer's signed mean of half the forward-minus-backward lateral signal.

| Time per line (s) | Average friction (V) | File |
|---|---|---|
| 0.1 | 0.000404 | `lfm_loc300486.nid` |
| 0.075 | 0.000393 | `lfm_loc300487.nid` |
| 0.05 | 0.000375 | `lfm_loc300488.nid` |

Friction drops slightly as the scan gets faster.

The height data in all three files changes steadily across the frame, from about 4.2 µm at the first line to about −0.59 µm at the last. This could be drift or settling, but I did not check whether it affects the friction values.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

## Feedback gain and setpoint settings

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

## Operating modes

`application.OperatingMode.OperatingMode` is a readable/writable mode selector.
The connection's `OperatingMode` enumeration includes `StaticAFM`, `DynamicAFM`,
`PhaseContrast`, and `LateralForce`. This reference does not select a mode for a task.

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

## Feedback gain and setpoint settings

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Operating modes

`application.OperatingMode.OperatingMode` is a readable/writable mode selector.
The connection's `OperatingMode` enumeration includes `StaticAFM`, `DynamicAFM`,
`PhaseContrast`, and `LateralForce`. This reference does not select a mode for a task.

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

AFM API reference (managed-afm-v2)

## Feedback gain and setpoint settings

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

messages.content:
All three lateral-force acquisitions finished with the requested settings, and each was analysed. The roughness values are probably inflated by an artefact rather than reflecting the surface, though.

**Height artefact.** Each frame's first rows start at about +4.4 µm and settle to about −0.63 µm further down the frame. This looks like a settling or drift transient after the switch into contact mode, not real topography. It is likely the main cause of the large Rq (about 900 nm) and Ra (about 470 nm). These are values from the unlevelled height data, so I have not corrected them. A fourth frame after settling, or levelling the data, would likely give much smaller roughness.

**Low friction.** Average friction magnitude is very small in all three frames, about 0.0004 V.

**Settings used.** The instrument was switched from PhaseContrast to LateralForce mode. All three frames used a 5 × 5 µm area at 256 × 256 pixels, 0.075 s per line and a 0.1 V setpoint. P/I/D gains were 100/50/0. The centre (0, 0) and rotation (0°) were left unchanged, and the three frames were taken back to back with no parameter changes.

**Calculation.** Roughness is computed from the forward Z-Axis (height) channel and reported in nm. Friction is half of forward minus backward on the friction channel, averaged as a magnitude, in V.

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

All three acquisitions are complete and analyzed with identical parameters. Before giving the values, there is a data-quality problem you should know about.

**Height-channel artifact:** every frame starts with a large Z excursion. The height falls from about +4.4 µm in the first lines to about −0.53 µm by the end of the frame. This looks like a Z-feedback settling transient or a strong sample tilt, not real surface features. Because the roughness metric uses unlevelled data, this excursion dominates the result. The reported Rq (~890 nm) and Ra (~470 nm) therefore mostly reflect this drift, not the true surface roughness. Since the same pattern repeats in all three frames, simply rescanning would not fix it.

**Friction signal:** the mean friction magnitude is very small, about 0.35–0.41 mV, close to zero.

**Repeatability:** the three images agree closely with each other, so the scans are consistent even though the roughness values are inflated.

## Feedback gain and setpoint settings

`application.ZController` exposes `PGain`, `IGain`, `DGain`, `SetPoint`, and
`SetPointForceUnitMode`. The setpoint unit depends on the operating mode. Amplitude
setpoints are percentages; for voltage setpoints, `SetPointForceUnitMode` is 0.

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Frame acquisition and completion

`application.Scan.StartFrameUp()` and `StartFrameDown()` each acquire one frame.
The adapter waits for a fresh, stable, parseable NID and an idle scanner, then
returns the absolute file path. `acquire_frame(direction="up")` is an equivalent
adapter entry point accepting `"up"` or `"down"`. Instrument calls are serialized.
`Scan.Stop()` stops activity. Continuous scanning, Pause, manual capture, and
changing the output directory are unavailable through this adapter.
`application.SetGalleryHistoryFilenameMask(prefix)` accepts a filename prefix,
not a directory. InstrumentUnavailable denotes failed infrastructure; ScriptError
reports a code error after successful cleanup and a health check.

## Scan geometry and resolution settings

`application.Scan` exposes `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, `CenterPosX`, and
`CenterPosY` in metres; `Rotation` in degrees; `Points` and `Lines` as counts;
and `Scantime` in seconds per line. Properties are readable and writable while idle.

The three acquisitions are done, but the height data shows a large transient that I can't rule out as an artifact. The first rows of each Z image sit near +4.4 µm and fall by about 0.18 µm per line before levelling off near −0.47 µm. That is about a 5 µm range, which is unusual for a 5 µm scan and looks like feedback or Z settling at the start of each frame. Because roughness is computed from unlevelled height, it dominates the reported Rq (~876–889 nm) and Ra (~460–468 nm). These may not reflect true surface roughness. The values are consistent across the three scans, so the effect is repeatable, but I did not investigate its cause or acquire extra frames to check.

All three frames used Lateral Force mode with the specified parameters: 5 µm × 5 µm, 256 × 256, 0.075 s per line, setpoint 0.1 V, P/I/D 100/50/0. Scan centre (0, 0) and rotation 0° were unchanged, and nothing was changed between scans. Friction is the mean magnitude of half the forward-minus-backward lateral signal, in V. It is very small (~0.0002 V) and decreases slightly from scan 1 to scan 3.
